paper_metadata.title: Strength-ductility synergy of Al0.3CoCrFeNiCu high-entropy alloy via cold rolling and subsequent annealing

The as-cast sample displays a typical interdendritic structure, which is elongated along the rolling direction (RD) after rolling treatment ( Fig. 1 c-d).
The chemical compositions of matrix and interdendritic structure indicate Cu-segregation at the inter-dendritic regions ( Table 1 ).
The CR sample shows the elongated grains without recrystallization, and the boundaries of matrix and Cu-rich phases are still clear ( Fig. 1 d).
The CRR sample exhibits fully recrystallized grains with the size of ~ 1 to 1.5 μm, smaller than that of Cu-rich region with lager grain size of ~2 to 8 μm ( Fig. 1 e)

The contributing yield stress of precipitations is ~ 126 MPa for L12 phases [24].
Consequently, the combined contribution of grain size and L12 precipitates to the CRR-600 sample can be estimated to be ~ 966 MPa.
